rows.title_full: AN ACT EXTENDING THE DUTY-FREE SHOPPING PRIVILEGES OF OVERSEAS CONTRACT WORKERS FROM ONE THOUSAND DOLLARS ($1,000.00) TO TWO THOUSAND DOLLARS ($2,0000.00) ANNUALLY WHICH MAY BE AVAILED OF EVEN PRIOR TO THE ARRIVAL OF THE WORKERS IN THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Rationale: There is a social cost borne by Filipino families who must reluctantly send off their loved ones in search of greener pastures abroad.  It is the government's job to help minimize this social cost. As it is, the present duty-free privilege scheme allows the OCWs to avail of the privilege only upon their return to the Philippines, normally after two years' stint.  It is proposed that the said privilege be made available to them even prior to their return.  Small as it is, this proposal is one way of minimizing the social cost for it helps raise the self-esteem of the Overseas Contract Workers' (OCWs).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 1997-01-21

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 69 OF BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 881, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE OMNIBUS ELECTION CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES (nuisance candidate)
rows.abstract: Rationale: The measure aims to uphold the integrity of elections by prohibiting nuisance candidates, as defined under this proposed measure, to participate in any electoral exercise and cause confusion to the electorate. Contains these key features:(1) those who use a similar name as the registered candidates; (2) those who have no bona fide intention to run as a candidate for an electoral; and (3) those who have been defeated in at least three (3) successive elections of the same elective position.

rows.title_full: AN ACT APPROPRIATING P40 BILLION IN ADDITIONAL CAPITAL FOR THE BANGKO SENTRAL NG PILIPINAS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Under Republic Act 7653 (The New Central Bank Act), the central monetary authority has a capitalization of P50 billion. > However, the government has so far provided only P10 billion for its capital.> BSP Gov. Gabriel C. Singson has urged the national government to infuse the additional P40 billion for its capitalization or its ability to maintain stability, particularly controlling inflation, would be affected.  In its year-end report the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas said "a strong capital baseis essential to the continuing ability and credibility of the BSP to do its job well of preserving financial stability.
rows.status: Substituted by HR01162

rows.title_full: AN ACT ALLOWING FILIPINO CITIZENS RESIDING OR WORKING ABROAD TO EXERCISE THEIR RIGHT OF SUFFRAGE, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: "Absentte Voting Act of 1997" Rationale: There are about 6 million Filipinos working or residing abroad.  They are considered one of the top dollar earners.  They deserve to be given a voice in determining the leaders who shall shape and steer the nation's future, including policies and programs tht will affect them. > Provides for these areas of concern: (1) Absentee Voting Rights, Scope; (2) Application and Registration of Voters; (3) Report and Transmission of Ballots; (4) Canvass of Absentee Votes; etc. > Covers the following --- (1)  Overseas contract workers employed in foreign countries and their Filipino dependents who are living with them; (2) Employees of the Philippine government assigned in foreign countries, and their Filipinoo spouses and dependents who are living with them; and (3) Filipino citizens who are legal immigrants or temporary residents of foreign countries, and their Filipino spouses and dependents who are living with them.
rows.status: Substituted by HB09396

rows.abstract: Rationale: Only by recognizing the heroic struggle of the people of Mindanao against colonial rule and by declaring as national heroes the Mindanaoans who fought so that this nation may be free and independent can we achieve a truthful and truly national celebration of the Philippine Centennial and the unity of the entire Filipino people.> It is high time that we correct the injustice inflicted on our brothers in the South. Now is the opportune time to give recognition where it is due.  This bill, if enacted into law, will make our celebration of the Centennial of the Philippine Independence truly national and complete.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROHIBIT THE IMPORTATION OF TOXIC WASTES AND SUBSTANCES INTO THE COUNTRY
rows.abstract: Rationale: The industries of the world's richest countries produce limmions of tons of highly poisonous waste products annually. Many of these unwanted poisons are dumped in developing countries becuase of their more tolerant environmental laws. Industrialized countries pay the world's poorer nations to reprocess hazardous wastes in what is now called the "Toxic Waste Trade." "Toxic Substance Control Act of 1996"  Seeks to correct weakness in the legal system of the country which would enable it to deal with the problem of "toxic waste trafficking." Declares  the following --- "SEC. 6. PROHIBITION. - The importation of toxic wastes or substances shall hereby be prohibited. For this purpose, the Commissioner of customs shall refuse entry off such importation within the Philippine customs territory.  As used in this Section, 'Customs Territory' shall include the territorial air and sea boundaries of the country."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 1997-01-27

rows.abstract: Rationale: This bill intends to provide a mechanism different sectors of our educational system can equally exercise their rrights to express their positions in any proposed increase in the rate of tuition and/or other school fees. Furthermore, apart from financial statements, the school administration is required to submit expansion and wage increase plans for faculty and non-faculty members, among others. rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE USE OF SEAT BELTS IN ALL VEHICLES AND PRESCRIBING A PENALTY FOR VIOLATION THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Provides for the following --- :Section 1. Mandatory Installation of Seat Belts - All manufacturers, assemblers or importers of all types of motor vehicle in the country shall hereby be mandated to install seatbelts in all their manufactured, assembled or imported motor vehicles.  The number of seatblets to be installed shall be according to the rated passenger capacity of each motor vehicle." "Section 2. Penalty.- The officer, director, manager of the motor vehicle manufacturer, assembler, orimporter who fails to comply with the provision of this Act shall be punished by imprisonment of not less than one year. In addition, the operating license of the manufacturer, assembler, or importer shall be revoked."
